title: Titles on the 'Queen of Song' album; Claude Hopkins and 'I Thought About You'
summary: Songs on the album, the traditional set with Claude Hopkins, and memories tied to 'I Thought About You'.

I was mentioning before, July of 1969.

are: 'A Hundred Years From Today', 'As Long As I Live',

And, of course, the others were done actually at the Manassas jazz festival.
One especially that's interesting is the one I did with Claude Hopkins and Danny Barker on guitar, Van Perry on bass, and Freddy Moore on drums, and Wally Garner --
The all time --
Yeah, clarinets.
And this is real traditional jazz. And we do "St. Louis Blues" with Count Basie -- Joe Williams ending "Every Day, Every Day, Every Day."
That really is one of your most walking performances on the stage.
Yeah, it really swings. I like that.
"I Thought About You" is one that I like to do. It's old, it's a good tune that I like to sing. I got that in my repertoire now.
I think most people associate that with Frank Sinatra --
Yes, they do.
Speaking of nostalgia, they get very

quiet for this one, because I think they remember -- This was a song that came out during the war. It's a beautiful tune and I like it.
It brings back a lot of memories.

Yeah, it brings back a lot of memories. And, of course, there's 'Every Time, Every Time I Fall In Love Again.' 'Georgia' -- after I did 'Georgia' on the Hoagy Carmichael album, that became pretty much part of my standard repertoire now. And, 'A Hundred Years From Today' -- boy, I remember 'A Hundred Years From Today' from Ella Waters -- Ethel Waters recorded it years ago. And I remember Mildred Bailey recording it. I've always liked 'A Hundred Years From Today.' And it has become a favorite now. And the rest are, 'I'm Coming Virginia' which is on the other side of the original recording of 'Loch Lomond.' 'I've Got A Right To Sing The Blues' --
